'''{{'}}Mamphono Khaketla''' (born 5 March 1960) is a [[Lesotho]] [[mathematician]] and [[senator]] who served as [[Ministry of Finance (Lesotho)|Minister of Finance]] from March 2015 to June 2017.

==Early life and education==
Khaketla was born in [[Maseru]] on 5 March 1960 to Bennett Makalo and [[Caroline Ntseliseng ’Masechele Khaketla]].<ref name=ADM>{{cite book|title=African Doctorates in Mathematics: A Catalogue|publisher=Lulu.com|year=2007|page=147}}</ref> Her father was a novelist, journalist, politician and former minister, as well as the major shareholder of Mohlabani Property Company, and left her a sizeable estate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lestimes.com/minister-wins-back-fathers-estate/|title=Minister wins back father's estate|work=Lesotho Times|date=29 September 2011|accessdate=16 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sundayexpress.co.ls/khaketla-estate-wrangle-rages-on/|title=Khaketla estate wrangle rages on|work=Sunday Express|date=10 December 2010|accessdate=16 May 2017}}</ref> Her mother was a teacher and author, one of the first women published in Lesotho.<ref name=HD>{{cite book|title=Historical Dictionary of Lesotho|pages=204–205|first1=Scott|last1=Rosenberg|first2=Richard F.|last2=Wesifelder|publisher=Scarecrow Press|year=2013|isbn=9780810879829|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=B2TWVN92hYYC}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Historical Dictionary of Women in Sub-Saharan Africa|page=146|first=Kathleen|last=Sheldon|publisher=Rowman & Littlefield|year=2016|isbn=9781442262935|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HwqQCwAAQBAJ}}</ref>

Khaketla did her primary and secondary schooling Maseru, before receiving a [[Bachelor of Education]] from the [[National University of Lesotho]] in 1980.<ref name=HD/> She has a master's degree in education and a [[PhD]] in [[mathematics education]] from the [[University of Wisconsin]] (1991).<ref name=HD/> Her thesis was titled "An analysis of the Lesotho Junior Certificate Mathematics Examination and its impact on instructions".<ref name=ADM/>

==Career==
Khaketla was a lecturer in [[mathematics]] at the National Teacher Training College from 1981 until 1995 and became assistant director of the college.<ref name=HD/> She worked at the Institute of Development Management in Lesotho and [[Botswana]] from 1996 until 2001 before becoming the director of the Centre for Accounting Studies.

Khaketla was appointed as a senator by [[List of Prime Ministers of Lesotho|Prime Minister]] [[Pakalitha Mosisili]] in 2002 and served as Minister of Communications, Science and Technology from 2002 until 2004.<ref name=HD/> At the [[2007 Lesotho general election|2007 election]], she lost her seat but was elected to the [[National Assembly (Lesotho)|National Assembly]] as one of the [[Lesotho Congress for Democracy]] members on a party list for [[proportional representation]] submitted by the National Independence Party.<ref name=HD/> She served as Minister of Education and Training from 2007 until 2012. In 2011, Khaketla was one of seven women ministers in the Cabinet, alongside: [[Mannete Ramaili|Mannete Ramali]], [[Maphoka Motoboli]], [[Mathabiso Lepono]], [[Mphu Keneileo Ramatlapeng]], [[Mpeo Mahase-Moiloa]] and [[Pontso Suzan Matumelo Sekatle]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/politicalhandboo0000unse_a2s3/page/832|title=Political handbook of the world 2012|date=2012|publisher=Sage|editor=Lansford, Tom |isbn=978-1-4522-3434-2|location=Los Angeles|pages=832|oclc=794595888}}</ref> On 30 March 2015 she was appointed [[Ministry of Finance (Lesotho)|Minister of Finance]].

In November 2015, she presided over the 102nd session of the [[African, Caribbean and Pacific Group of States]] Council of Ministers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acp.int/content/statement-president-102nd-session-acp-council-ministers-hon-dr-mamphono-khaketla-minister-fi|title=Statement by the President of the 102nd session of the ACP Council of Ministers, Hon. Dr. Mamphono Khaketla, Minister of Finance of Lesotho|date=24 November 2015|place=Brussels|publisher=ACP|accessdate=16 May 2017}}</ref>

In July 2016, Khaketla was accused of soliciting a bribe for a major government contract in a case that was before the courts. She denied the allegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://city-press.news24.com/News/lesothos-great-car-con-20160813|title=Lesotho's great car 'con'|first=Keiso|last=Mohloboli|work=City Press|date=14 August 2016|accessdate=16 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=DC Youths blast Minister|work=Lesotho Times|date=28 July 2016|accessdate=16 May 2017|first=Lekhetho|last=Ntsukunyane|url=https://www.pressreader.com/lesotho/lesotho-times/20160728/281479275781204}}</ref>
